title: The Half-Platform Problem
premise: A conductor must connect two half-length platforms, but differently divided tiles make the lengths look unequal. Sliding both onto the same unit rail reveals equivalent fractions and completes the bridge.
visible_action: Fraction tiles slide along a fixed rail; subdivision marks appear without changing either tile length.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Equivalent fractions describe the same amount when the whole stays fixed.
gate: Keep the reference whole identical and verify every tile length.

editorial_pick.original_reason: Equivalent fractions can be seen directly. A fixed reference rail makes the central comparison easy to inspect.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Two original platform tiles slide onto one shared unit rail. Use a brief prediction, the reveal and a clear final hold.
editorial_pick.gate: Check all lengths and subdivisions mathematically. Keep one reference whole throughout.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
